correctness.rationale: From the cited pure-noise zero formula, equality of first intensities is exactly an affine difference of log Gaussian convolutions. Gaussian-weighted PSD measures have entire Laplace transforms; equality on real arguments extends to imaginary arguments and gives a translated positive measure by Fourier uniqueness. Undoing the weights yields the precise orbit with factor a²/(8π). A two-sided polynomial lower bound rules out nonzero a by exponential-growth contradiction, while compact supports demonstrate failure without that hypothesis. The constant-intensity converse follows by quadratic moment-generating function and polynomial-growth exclusion. The numerical checker separately validates convolution and variance identities; it is not the proof.

value.rationale: Exactly characterizes when a natural stochastic Fourier zero statistic identifies its underlying colored-noise PSD, without imposing two arbitrary smoothed-spectrum integration constants. It gives a broad polynomial-tail uniqueness regime and an explicit arbitrarily disjoint spectral-band nonidentifiability mechanism at the opposite extreme, plus a complete classification of homogeneous zero density. These are motivated structural inverse facts with direct interpretation for zero-based spectral inference, not an arbitrary finite computation.
